input().value: The starting value, whose type decides the kind of row: a number gives a number field, `true` or `false` a tick box, text a text field, a colour a swatch, and a price series such as `close` a menu of price sources. It must be known before any data arrives.
input().title: The row's label in the settings dialog, written as text at the call. When the input is assigned to a name it may be left out, and the name becomes the label.
input().min: For a number, the lowest value allowed. The arrows stop there, and a saved value below it stops the study from loading with `OS6019`.
input().max: For a number, the highest value allowed. The arrows stop there, and a saved value above it stops the study from loading with `OS6019`.
input().step: For a number, how far one click of an arrow moves the value. It shapes the arrows only: a value typed into the field is kept as typed.
input().options: A list of strings that turns a text row into a menu of exactly those values. The default must be one of them, or the script is refused with `OS3018`.
input().kind: Picks a row the type alone cannot: `"interval"` builds a timeframe menu, and `"time"` a date and time field whose value is a timestamp. `"symbol"`, `"price"` and `"session"` are planned, and writing one is error `OS2001`.
input().group: A heading the row sits under. The settings dialog, and the input forms of the Backtest and Strategies panels, show each group as a heading over its rows.
input().tooltip: Help text shown as a line under the row: the unit, or what moving the value does.
input().inline: Planned: rows given the same value would sit on one line. It is accepted and has no effect yet.
input().confirm: Planned: the value would be asked for when the study is added to a chart. It is accepted and has no effect yet.
